summary: A text field that filters a list of options down to one selected value.
useWhen: the list is long enough that scanning it is worse than typing
the user picks exactly one value from a known set
the options carry a second line of context the native <select> cannot render

useInstead.when: the list is short and fully scannable
useInstead.why: the native control brings keyboard handling and the mobile platform picker for free; this rebuilds all of it

useInstead.when: there are two or three mutually exclusive choices worth showing at once
the value is free text and the list is only a convenience
useInstead.why: or set `allowsCustomValue`, which is the same decision made explicitly

useInstead.when: the rows are commands rather than values
useInstead.why: options are selected and stay selected; menu items are invoked and the menu closes

guarantees: role=combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant, from react-aria's useComboBox
real focus never leaves the input; arrow keys move a virtual focus through the list, which is what keeps typing and browsing possible at once
the popover is non-modal, so the page behind stays readable and focus stays in the field
Escape reverts to the last committed value rather than clearing the field
filtering is Intl.Collator-based, so accents and locale-specific casing behave correctly
the empty message is a sibling of the listbox, not an option in it, so it is never counted, focused or selectable
the menu matches the field's width, clamped to the space right of it so a full-bleed field cannot push the menu past the viewport edge
requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered
`emptyLabel` wording that says why nothing is listed, if the default is too terse

antiPatterns.dont: giving the disclosure button a tab stop
antiPatterns.why: the input already opens the list with ArrowDown. A second tab stop doubles the cost of tabbing past every combobox in a form and adds nothing

antiPatterns.dont: styling the focused option with :hover or :focus
antiPatterns.why: no option is ever either — focus is virtual. Use [data-focused], which react-aria sets for both pointer and keyboard

antiPatterns.dont: posting the input's text in a form
antiPatterns.why: the text is the label and the value is the key; pass `name` and the component posts the key in a hidden input
it fails on accents and on Turkish dotted/dotless I, silently, in the locales least likely to be tested

antiPatterns.dont: writing a width onto the menu from a ResizeObserver or any effect that runs while it is open
antiPatterns.why: a positioned popover that changes size feeds back into react-aria's positioning, and any scrollbar that results is read by useCloseOnScroll as a real scroll. The menu opens and closes within about a hundred milliseconds, which presents as a keyboard bug rather than a layout one

emptyLabel.expects: what to show when the filter matches nothing
